newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish pound follows in footsteps of wavering stg.
newsitem.headline: Irish pound follows in footsteps of wavering stg.

text.p: The Irish pound stayed close to sterling in morning trade on Wednesday as the UK currency jumped to 30-month highs against the mark before it slipped back towards its opening levels, dealers said.
They said the punt was expected to stick to tight ranges against the British currency although a break on the upside was possible if expectations of an interest rate hike in Britain began to wane.
"Sterling has come off a little bit from its morning highs," one dealer said. "In the past few days we've been trading in a very narrow range against sterling and that's continuing."
By 1220 GMT the Irish pound was at 1.0027 stg, barely changed from Tuesday's close of 1.0019. It was at 2.5200 marks and $1.6810 versus 2.5220 marks and $1.6783.
Dealers said British M4 data had been stronger than expected while UK October retail sales figures were largely in line with forecasts.
Sterling hit a four-year high versus the dollar and 30-month high against the mark in anticipation of strong data but later gave up its gains.

"The retail sales figures were much as expected but I think secretly some people were expecting higher numbers which would have confirmed their expectations of a UK rate hike, maybe even before Christmas," one dealer said.
He said sterling's current strength was unlikely to push the punt below parity as the central bank would intervene to support it around this level.

"We've seen good support for the Irish pound at parity and it's going to be a tough nut to crack," the dealer said. "(The central bank) seem determined to maintain parity and they have a lot of reserves to play with."
"There's more chance of a break on the topside, if expectations of a UK rate hike begin to fade and sterling positions begin to unravel," he said.
Dealers said next week's UK budget was the next big focus for the Irish currency market.
